experiences.text: Dismiss nitpicks about hardcoded regex lists or synchronization hazards during bug fixes.

Lead with concrete cross-surface silent-failure bugs — cache keys that omit the taxonomy, empty-set vs None key aliasing, enforce-mode fail-closing the dominant PRA-REVIEW type, half-enabled flag states — since these convergent, reward-impacting failure modes are the only findings on this repo that reviewers reliably treat as actionable.
Confirm that new configuration parsing features do not inadvertently bypass security validations.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Do not re-litigate the removed gate's threat model (author-manufacturable LLM failures, replacement breakers) — it was explicitly settled in review #188 and humans dismiss such challenges on this PR.

Keep PRA-MAINTAINABILITY only for duplication directly visible in the diff, like PRA_VERSION pasted into both touchstone workflows with a comment admitting manual sync, and state the single-source fix inline.

Lead with concrete, verifiable behavioral risks — suppress semantics that could hard-discard real bugs, renumbering that breaks Pattern-N references, missing external-boundary carve-outs — because humans act on findings that name a specific failure mode and file.
Note silent regressions where a default-value flip silently degrades behavior for existing deployments without any warning or changelog entry.

Keep PRA-MAINTAINABILITY suppressed for data chores — the repo's own experience store carries multi-PR evidence for this suppression, and idempotency/reproducibility lectures in these -3.5/-4.0 reviews were ignored.
Refrain from auditing implementation-level security measures based solely on documentation text.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Do not flag mixed language comments unless the repository has a strict English-only policy.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

Add a unit test pinning the unset-TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS warning to the imported runner constant (not the literal '128000') and check whether any existing test still asserts the old '32768' string, since missing coverage is precisely why this drifted.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Drop speculative repo-wide grep demands for a hypothetical fourth marker emission site unless a concrete call point is named, since unfounded completeness sweeps read as filler.

Cap PRA-ROBUSTNESS at one diff-verifiable failure mode per review, because stacking four hypotheticals (force-push races, masked git adds, stranded branches, silent variable renames) makes humans dismiss the whole pile.
Skip relitigating the causal direction of pre-existing prose (超窗 vs 裁空) inside the untouched message wording; reviewers treat this as second-guessing rather than a reviewable defect.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.

不要对测试断言品味发表流程性批评——如上限从 500 放宽到 600 是『第二次让步』、count('
') 断言偏脆——人类把这类意见视为主观偏好而不采纳。

Suppress test-brittleness and coverage-breadth nitpicks (hardcoded 'MUST be one of' prompt substrings, shared-constant extraction, stub-routing anchors, 'add one more test' asks) — they recur in every review of this learning-loop repo yet humans dismiss them as churn, and restraint on test-only diffs is what earns reward.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.
Ensure API error handling fails explicitly rather than returning empty strings to prevent false negatives in security scans.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.
Suppress warnings about platform compatibility heuristics that are covered by explicit configuration checks.
Avoid escalating the Secrets→Variables migration into speculative fork-PR context bugs or vars-vs-secrets visibility theories; fold any such concern into the existing request for CI evidence instead.

Request the committed cleanup script plus kept/deleted ID manifests with the retention predicate, and — unique to the top-rewarded review — verify the purge explicitly skipped locked:true entries, which this store maintains precisely to protect accepted experience.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Skip scope-expanding redesign questions such as removing setup-python's pip cache entirely instead of the mkdir shim, because reviewers don't act on alternative-architecture comments in a hotfix PR.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress suggestions to make anti-drift tests robust against the specific structural variations they are designed to detect and prevent.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Never report trailing whitespace or inconsistent backtick formatting in README tables; these markdownlint-level nits are dismissed by humans.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Drop README-mirroring, comment-drift, and docs-update findings (PRA-DOC/PRA-DOCS); humans do not act on documentation notes on CI wiring PRs.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not request documentation updates for simple configuration downgrades or internal security fixes that do not change user-facing behavior.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.
Skip meta-asks like verifying the review_reliable=False rationale or adding a changelog entry for the removed gate — reviewers ignore narrative-verification and changelog requests here.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.
Avoid criticizing design decisions for report truncation limits or demanding user-facing indicators for 'big PR caps'.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.

Lead with accuracy findings whenever renamed positioning contradicts the repo's own stated semantics — here 'AI Committer' implies merge authority while the README itself says AI review is advisory, the only gate is a deterministic non-LLM check, and autonomy defaults off — so quote the contradicting lines and propose safe wording (e.g., AI Reviewer) that preserves the product's trust model.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.

Demand attached evidence, such as a workflow run proving identical env resolution including the empty-value fallback, for any 'zero behavior change' assertion in release notes instead of accepting it on trust.

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Include the advisory that with a true 128000 fallback, leaving TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS unset will 400 on sub-128k models, but frame it as optional/deferred rather than blocking the text fix.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Open release-PR reviews by verifying that every change the changelog attributes to another PR (e.g. #216) is actually merged with green CI into the tagged tree before the version bump lands.
Flag concrete, in-diff CHANGELOG breakage like missing Keep-a-Changelog link definitions or compare ranges that must not point at the skipped v0.3.4 tag — authors fix these immediately.

Explicitly credit correct release hygiene, like the single-source dynamic version bump and clean relocation of the pending changelog section, since top-rated reviews pair scrutiny with acknowledgment.
Skip speculative 'verify runner behavior and document trade-offs' asks (empty-commit round classification, squash-merge) that fall outside a docs-only PR's scope.
Omit PRA-CLAIM-VERIFICATION re-checks of latency and timeout measurements; fold any measurement question into the existing stale-comment item instead of a separate entry.
Omit post-merge release mechanics advice about tag naming and publish-workflow triggers — it lives outside the diff and gets dismissed.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.

Stop relitigating patch-vs-minor bumps for additive artifact fields or demanding full field schemas on release PRs — maintainers dismiss versioning pedantry when the changelog already discloses the addition.
Drop wording audits of '契约零变化'-style claims that hinge on zero-change vs no-breaking-change distinctions; humans treat these as semantic quibbles on a release-only diff and ignore them.

Surface fail-closed activation as a consumer-visible ops change in the release notes — pipelines that previously passed on engine errors may now block — and point to the config switch or downgrade path.

Since this project's releases repeatedly promise copy alignment, cross-check every string the changelog quotes (touchstone:converged, 未知决策态) against the actual code constants so the release notes don't create fresh copy drift.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Do not demand companion tests for adjacent branches (missing skill path, packaging validation of the deployed SKILL.md) when the PR's stated goal is just making the existing regression test hermetic — scope-expanding coverage asks were penalized.

Lead with concrete contract bugs: check that orchestrator._max_diff_lines actually implements the comment's claimed semantics (unset vs empty-string vs '0') and that container/env-allowlist layers don't strip TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES before delivery.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.

Stop emitting PRA-PREVENT items — the root-cause/allowlist point already lands under PRA-CORRECTNESS, and the type was absent from the highest-reward review while adding only redundant re-wordings in every lower-reward one.
Omit PRA-COVERAGE survivor-set audits — it surfaced only in the lowest-rewarded review and reads as padding once the manifest-and-predicate ask already covers verifying which 11 entries survived.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

Recompute every quantitative claim in release changelogs (passed+skipped versus claimed totals, net-new counts) and report contradictions as PRA-MAJOR — the 1239+11=1250 vs 1250→1278 test-count mismatch is the one finding every reviewer repeats and authors must fix before tagging.
Keep the 'why was 0.3.4 burned' request to a one-clause changelog wording fix; a brief factual note is all maintainers will act on.
Do not label version-bump-only release PRs as blockers because the fix "isn't in the diff" — the fix ships via companion PR #212 and reviewers dismiss empty-release accusations as noise.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.

Always require a dedicated 变更/修复 entry for every PR claimed in the release header — the missing #218 preflight-copy item under [0.3.7] was the one gap all three top-reward reviewers independently flagged.

For Keep a Changelog bracketed headers, always check the file bottom for the new compare-link definition and the advanced [未发布] range, since a missing '[0.3.7]: ...compare/v0.3.6...v0.3.7' renders as a dead link and every high-reward review raised it.
Treat the PR count, PR numbers, and hardcoded release date as falsifiable claims and verify them against git log v0.3.6..HEAD and the actual tag date instead of restating the header.

For touchstone/__init__.py version bumps, demand concrete release evidence: grep for leftover hardcoded '0.3.6' (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, CI), confirm dynamic --version resolves to the new value, and check tag/GitHub Release follow-through.
Flag internal review-process narration ('评审 3 轮收敛…边界收口') in user-facing changelog text, asking it be moved to the PR description and replaced with user-observable behavior bullets.

Do not invent hypothetical parser breakage like 'if tooling/tests parse the ## [x.y.z] — date pattern' without citing an actual regex or CI check in this repo — only the lowest-reward review raised such speculation and it was dismissed.

Treat every deleted README section as a migration audit: enumerate the unique operational facts that vanish (touchstone doctor self-check, dry-run command, .touchstone/ policy-config pointer, TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR isolation for concurrent runs, touchstone-metrics.json, Secrets→Variables dual-read fallback) and require the author to confirm each is covered in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md or restore a one-line pointer instead of wholesale deletion.

Flag internal contradictions between the new title, tagline, and body scope (English 'Committer' vs Chinese '检视', 'AI 生成的代码' vs review of all PRs) so the positioning converges on one accurate statement used consistently repo-wide.

Suppress changelog phrasing nits — the '（用户指示）' process annotation, merging duplicate simplification entries, changelog still describing the deleted scale numbers — since the highest-reward review omitted CHANGELOG entirely and authors dismiss process-level nitpicks on a user-directed cleanup PR.

Do not push to restore deleted rationale sentences, brand wordplay (试金石 double meaning), or trust-model explanations against an explicitly user-directed simplification; at most suggest relocating them to docs/, because the lowest-reward reviews spent their slots on this 'add back what was deleted' guidance and it was not acted on.

Lead with runtime changes buried in docs-typed PRs — TOUCHSTONE_LLM_REFLECT_MODEL flips and the SIZE-001 gate default 1000→3000 in touchstone.yml that downstream repos copy verbatim — and demand a split PR or explicit retitle as the review's headline action.

Flag every CHANGELOG/workflow-comment claim (orchestrator._max_diff_lines=3000, warning text, synced tests, e2e glm-5.3 fallback) that has no corresponding code or test file visible in the diff, and require the author to confirm those changes ship in this PR.

Call out workflow comments whose rationale now contradicts the shipped values, such as '自评是浅任务,小模型即可' justifying glm-4.7 or the glm-5.2-measured 3600s timeout sitting beside a glm-5.3 reference model.
Push to delete, date-stamp, or fuzzy the hardcoded volatile README stats (1286 用例/45 文件, 14100 行/39 模块, 91% 覆盖率, 8 条 workflow, v0.3.7) and point readers at doctor/CI output instead.

Insist the user-view README rewrite preserve or explicitly link operator-critical content (.touchstone/ config table, doctor/preflight, degraded-mode and fail-closed gate behavior) rather than silently dropping it.
Verify the README's headline promise of '3 分钟部署/不需要 fork 或 clone' against the actual copy-paste workflow template, required secrets/vars list, and intact .touchstone/ file references before merge.
Do not restate the default-vs-code mismatch under PRA-DOC-CODE-DRIFT when PRA-DOC-CODE-MISMATCH already covers the missing orchestrator/test changes.
Skip PRA-PR-TYPE-MISMATCH; the behavior-change-in-docs-PR finding already carries the split-or-retitle point and a second label just dilutes it.
Omit PRA-SCOPE-MIXED as a duplicate framing of the docs-PR-hiding-config-changes issue already raised prominently.
Do not file a separate policy-relaxation finding for the SIZE-001 1000→3000 raise; fold any token-budget arithmetic into the existing behavior-change note.
Avoid PRA-DEFAULT-POLICY-IMPACT as a redundant restatement of the gate-default loosening already flagged; at most append a one-line migration hint there.
Skip PRA-TEST-IMPACT since the test-sync question is already the core of the doc-code-mismatch finding; don't split it into its own item.
Omit PRA-CHANGELOG-ACCURACY as a duplicate audit of changelog claims already covered by the doc-code-mismatch check.
Drop speculative refactor suggestions like wiring TOUCHSTONE_LLM_REFLECT_MODEL through a repo variable; humans dismiss nice-to-have redesigns on a value-refresh PR.
Avoid demanding downstream migration notes as a standalone finding; derivable asks like this get ignored on template-refresh PRs.
Do not issue repo-wide sweep-for-old-values findings ('1000', glm-4.5-air, glm-5.2 elsewhere); blanket grep asks read as boilerplate and go unactioned.
Skip speculative endpoint-availability checks for glm-4.7/glm-5.3; hypothetical gateway gaps without evidence are dismissed by reviewers here.
Do not duplicate the stale-rationale point under PRA-COMMENT-RATIONALE-STALE when PRA-STALE-COMMENT already names the '小模型即可' contradiction.
Avoid restating the hardcoded-figures problem under PRA-STALE-STATS or PRA-DOC-ROT when PRA-NUMBERS-ROT already covers it once.
Do not file PRA-DOC-LOSS-OF-OPERATOR-INFO or PRA-DOCS-REGRESSION-RISK duplicates of the lost-operator-content concern; one PRA-INFO-LOSS finding with the concrete missing items is what gets acted on.

Import the fallback constant (e.g. DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS from touchstone/pr_agent_runner.py) and f-string it into both the preflight comment and the user-facing warning instead of hardcoding 128000, so the exact drift this PR fixes can never recur.

Since pr_agent_runner.py is not in the diff, cite the exact constant/line proving 128000 is the unconditional fallback and confirm no per-provider path still returns a different value before claiming 'alignment'.

Do not speculate that raising the fallback to 128000 worsens failure modes for small-window models or demand behavior redesign — humans fixing a copy-alignment PR dismiss out-of-scope semantics debates.
Drop nit-level comments such as verbatim motto-quoting mismatches between CHANGELOG and code comments or formatting of the pr_agent_runner.py citation — the top-rated reviews contain none of these.

Avoid suggesting severity reclassification (unset env should WARN instead of pass) or deferring to follow-up tickets; humans dismiss policy-change musings on an explicitly pre-existing behavior in a string-only fix.
Stop flagging missing Keep-a-Changelog compare-link references at the bottom of CHANGELOG.md; reviewers dismiss this bookkeeping on release PRs.
Drop checks that the hardcoded changelog date matches the eventual tag date; humans treat minor date drift as unavoidable and ignore it.
Suppress v-prefix tag-naming consistency warnings between PR titles, changelog headings, and compare links.
Skip nitpicks about the same migration phrase repeated in the heading, summary, and subsection of a changelog entry.

Do not demand repo-wide greps for hardcoded old versions, SECURITY.md matrix updates, or extra --version smoke checks when the version comes from a single dynamic source the top review already blessed as complete.

Flag documentation default changes only when they create a real behavioral contradiction with adjacent prose or recommended values, as in a default dropping from 8192 to 4096 while the text still claims truncation is avoided.
Do not demand migration of additional non-sensitive keys like model names beyond the PR's stated scope; at most note the inconsistency briefly instead of framing the doctrine as self-contradictory.
Skip speculative future-cleanup demands such as requiring TODO/issue anchors for dual-read fallbacks or proposing source-logging of env origins.
Do not nitpick docstring wording precision about migration-period fallback semantics when the workflow comments already document the behavior.
Do not speculate about registry artifacts or demand proof the skipped version was never published — reviewers cannot verify registry state from the diff and authors dismiss it.
Skip lectures on sequential-numbering conventions and remote tag/registry audits for the gap; after the changelog explains the skip, further investigation reads as noise.
Avoid asking the author to prove another merged PR's content or ancestry — cross-PR verification is out of scope for this diff and gets ignored.
Drop provenance demands that changelog entries trace to ancestor commits; humans treat merge-order bookkeeping as CI's job, not review feedback.
Omit 'confirm the release date and tag match' findings — unverifiable from the diff and universally dismissed.
Suppress critiques of empty-commit release mechanics and demands about pipeline guarantees — process opinions outside the diff are discounted by humans.
Do not split the same stale-version grep into separate findings per consumer (--version, metrics, SECURITY.md); repetition across findings is what drags review scores down.
In this repo the skill docs are the product, so correct any doc phrasing that teaches a false causal model (empty commit vs. push triggering review) with a concrete rewording.
Flag overstated guarantees in SKILL.md/render.py only when you can propose a concrete verify step (e.g. confirm comment posted before pushing) added to every source of truth.
Don't spend a finding on CHANGELOG heading/issue-reference conventions; humans treat these as reviewer taste and ignore them.

In release PRs, front-load concrete CHANGELOG mechanics: give the exact link-reference line to append (`[0.3.3]: .../compare/v0.3.2...v0.3.3`), the `[未发布]` baseline flip, and ask the author to verify the release date and the quoted regression-test count against reality.
Skip demands for closing keywords or merge-semantics clarification between issue #211 and PR #212; linkage bookkeeping gets dismissed when the changelog and PR title already name the issue.
Don't relitigate the "契约零变化" changelog claim or demand CI-run links and rewording of release notes; at most suggest one line of contract-test evidence in the PR description.
Omit generic release-mechanics boilerplate ("tag this exact commit", "keep CI green", "cut artifacts from the tagged tree") — release-PR authors know their own pipeline and dismiss it.

When a patch release adds fields to touchstone-findings.json, force the versioning decision explicitly: either bump to 0.4.0 or state in the changelog that the findings JSON is informational and not a stable contract.
Drop demands to attach pip-audit reports, hashed pins, or SBOM evidence for the PR-Agent venv upgrade — audit-trail boilerplate that maintainers dismiss on internal tool releases.
Skip supply-chain hardening suggestions (hashed requirements, SBOM recording) in changelog-and-version-bump release PRs; they belong in dedicated tooling work.
Omit process reminders like 'verify PR #208 is actually merged before tagging' — release managers already own tag-time gating and ignore such boilerplate.

Do not speculate about hypothetical strict consumers (additionalProperties:false validators, snapshot diffing, typed loaders) breaking on additive findings fields without evidence any such downstream exists in this repo.
Suppress compound re-verification essays (rerun the suite on the merge commit, check --version output, replace volatile counts with links) that just duplicate the single CI-link request.
Avoid grab-bag hygiene notes bundling docstring claims, SECURITY.md rendering, tag timing, and speculative markdown re-parenting into one comment — humans dismiss multi-part catch-alls.

Do not demand the release PR re-verify merged-PR/commit/test counts against git log and CI runs — the diff is only CHANGELOG plus a version bump, and reviewers dismiss such un-verifiable-in-diff checklist demands as noise.

Skip calls for a formal security advisory, CVE process, or SECURITY.md republishing inside a patch-release changelog PR — humans treat advisory logistics as out of scope and downgrade reviews that lead with them.
Do not invent operational follow-up risks like 'someone must merge the seed-experience PR or it silently stalls' — speculative ops storytelling about post-release workflow gets no uptake.
Do not stretch the 'zero change' critique into dependency-pinning semantics (exact versus lower-bound pr-agent pin) — this contract-lawyering is ignored by humans.
Do not demand per-claim regression-test citations to back absolute security wording in changelog prose — reviewers dismiss this as over-engineered unless a claim is flatly false.

Focus on the one check that decides whether the fix works: confirm the mkdir step's `if:` matches exactly what gates the venv-build skip, since restore-keys partial hits set cache-hit='false' and the original setup-python post-save failure then returns.

Drop speculative portability and internals hypotheticals (Windows/macOS shells, silent-fallback what-ifs, future action version bumps) that don't demonstrably reproduce on this repo's actual ubuntu runner.
Stop demanding the author confirm step ids or rerun extra cache branches that aren't visible in the diff, because these checklist-style 'please confirm' prompts get ignored.
Omit nice-to-have debuggability tweaks like echoing the resolved pip cache path, since humans dismiss logging nitpicks on targeted CI fixes.

Restrict PRA-CORRECTNESS to breakage provable from the diff itself, such as a workflow pip-install referencing pragent-constraints.txt that no commit in this PR creates, and drop 'possible double-persistence' hedges that need out-of-diff knowledge to confirm.
Never emit PRA-QUESTION why-interrogatives about pre-existing defaults such as hardcoded owner/repo fallbacks, as rhetorical questions register as filler and get skipped.
Demand this PR add or explicitly point to unit tests pinning the parser contract: missing → 1000, '' → 1000, '0' → disabled, valid integer, malformed value.
